title: Wi-Fi Troubleshooting: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Wi Fi is slow, or it keeps dropping. Where do you even start? Work through it in a set order.

scenes.heading: The noisy concert
scenes.narration: Imagine trying to chat in a loud concert venue. First check the device actually joins the network. Then check the signal, since below minus seventy five is poor. Then look for noise from other Wi Fi and other gadgets. Last, check the settings and how clients roam.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Common traps. Seeing the name doesn't prove the setup is right. More power can add interference. Having an address doesn't prove D H C P is right.

items.wrong: Seeing the SSID means the AP is fine
items.right: Other config can still be wrong

items.wrong: An IP address means DHCP is fine

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Wi-Fi troubleshooting lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Go in order: join, signal, interference, config. Below minus seventy five is a weak signal. More power isn't always better. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Wi-Fi troubleshooting lab.
